text:
linda-support: FYI customer ticket #45678 - dedicated pool dc-west-03 saw a ~3x throughput drop and spike in 503s starting ~14:05 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/cwq/dc-west-03

linda-support: quick snapshot from logs shows a huge fraction of tiny requests (1-3 tokens). pasted sample logs below:
```
[14:06:02] req_id=abc123 method=generate tokens=1 latency_ms=45 status=200
[14:06:02] req_id=abc124 method=generate tokens=1 latency_ms=78 status=200
[14:06:03] req_id=abc125 method=generate tokens=2 latency_ms=52 status=200
[14:06:05] req_id=abc200 method=generate tokens=1 latency_ms=310 status=503
```

sam-runtime: thanks. can we repro with many small requests to see batcher behavior? any non-prod replica we can hit?

linda-support: i put a quick curl loop that mimics the customer workload on staging: `for i in $(seq 1 1000); do curl -s -X POST https://staging-api/generate -d '{"prompt":"a","max_tokens":1}'; done`

devon-sre: ran your loop against a canary instance. batch formation histogram (1m window): size=1 -> 61%, size=2 -> 22%, size=3-4 -> 12%, size>=8 -> 5%. avg tokens per batch=1.4. queue_depth spiked but batches stayed small.

devon-sre: looks like continuous batcher is immediately flushing single-request batches because window_ms is too low for bursty tiny requests. that kills throughput — overhead per batch dominates.

sam-runtime: can we try bumping continuous_batcher.window_ms to 40ms on a single canary host and observe? that should let a few more requests accumulate and increase avg batch size.

maria-ctr: also check max_batch_tokens and per-request token counting logic. small requests can still get batched if we extend the wait. but we should avoid hurting p50 for latency-sensitive tenants. maybe apply only to this dedicated pool or add tenant-level batching_policy=throughput-first.

ops-bot: Deploy job started: apply-config dc-west-03/canary-01 (config change: continuous_batcher.window_ms=40)

ops-bot: Deploy finished: apply-config dc-west-03/canary-01 SUCCESS

devon-sre: after the change (5m sample): size=1 -> 28%, size=2 -> 34%, size=3-7 -> 30%, size>=8 -> 8%. avg tokens per batch=3.1. tokens/sec increased ~2.6x, p99 latency down ~45%. error 503s dropped to near zero.

linda-support: great, i'll update customer ticket #45678 with mitigation and ETA for roll-forward across pool. thanks team :tada:

maria-ctr: long term we should add per-tenant fair-queueing and an autoscale rule that considers effective tokens/sec not just inflight requests. also consider a heuristic for small-request tenants to get batched with a tiny delay rather than immediate flush.

sam-runtime: agreed. I'll open an RFC for "tenant-aware batching policies" and include telemetry hooks to detect noisy-tiny-request tenants.

devon-sre: added a short-lived metric: batch_efficiency = tokens_emitted / (batches * avg_batch_overhead_ms). will surface in console.

linda-support: thanks everyone. marking this thread resolved for now, will keep monitoring and will escalate if roll-forward doesn't stabilize across all nodes. :eyes:
